name: Insulin-Resistance Syndrome Type A
aliases: Severe Insulin Resistance Syndrome Type A

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Type A Insulin Resistance Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Severe insulin resistance evidenced by hyperinsulinemia disproportionate to glucose levels
Presence of acanthosis nigricans in typical locations such as the neck and axillae
Clinical or biochemical evidence of hyperandrogenism, including hirsutism or elevated serum androgens
Lack of obesity or minimal adiposity despite severe insulin resistance
Identification of heterozygous or homozygous mutations in the insulin receptor gene (INSR)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe insulin resistance with acanthosis nigricans and exclusion of other causes of insulin resistance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for INSR mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Marked hyperinsulinemia with normal or mildly elevated blood glucose
imaging: Polycystic ovarian morphology on pelvic ultrasound
Hepatic steatosis on abdominal ultrasound or MRI
other: Presence of acanthosis nigricans on physical examination
Absence of obesity despite severe insulin resistance

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with other autoimmune diseases
Abnormal fat distribution with loss of adipose tissue

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe insulin resistance with weight loss
Presence of autoimmune markers suggesting type B insulin resistance
references: OMIM Entry #608115 - Insulin Receptor, Type A Insulin Resistance
Taylor SI. Insulin Resistance Syndromes. In: Jameson JL, De Groot LJ, editors. Endocrinology: Adult and Pediatric. 7th ed. Elsevier; 2016.
